question: Which article of the constitution of India is related to Comptroller and Auditor General of India Audit reports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 151.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 151 of the Constitution of India deals with the audit reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) — reports relating to the accounts of the Union are submitted to the President, who lays them before each House of Parliament; reports relating to a State are submitted to the Governor, who lays them before the State Legislature. (अनुच्छेद 151 — नियंत्रक एवं महालेखा परीक्षक के लेखापरीक्षा प्रतिवेदन)

 

• Article 148 provides for the appointment, conditions of service, and removal of the CAG.

 

• Article 149 defines the duties and powers of the CAG in relation to the accounts of the Union and the States.

 

• Article 150 states that the accounts of the Union and States shall be kept in a form prescribed by the President on the advice of the CAG.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The CAG is often called the "guardian of the public purse" and is appointed under Article 148 for a term of 6 years or till age 65, whichever is earlier.

 

• CAG reports are scrutinised by the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) of Parliament.

 

NOTE

 

• 148 (Option 1): Deals with the appointment, oath, and removal of the CAG, not the audit reports themselves.

 

• 150 (Option 2): Deals with the form in which the accounts of the Union and States shall be kept.

 

• 149 (Option 4): Deals with the duties and powers of the CAG.

question: As on September 2021, which of the following is NOT a national political party in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indian National Lok Dal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As on September 2021, the Election Commission of India recognised eight national parties: BJP, INC, BSP, CPI, CPI(M), NCP, AITC (Trinamool Congress), and NPP (National People's Party, recognised in 2019).

 

• The Indian National Lok Dal (INLD) is a state/regional party based mainly in Haryana, founded by Devi Lal, and has never held national party status. (भारतीय राष्ट्रीय लोक दल — क्षेत्रीय दल)

 

• A party is granted "national party" status under the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968, based on vote-share and seat-winning criteria across multiple states.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• NCP and AITC later lost their national party status in an ECI review in 2023 (after this exam).

 

• The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) was granted national party status in April 2023.

 

NOTE

 

• Indian National Congress (Option 1): A recognised national party, one of India's oldest political parties.

 

• Communist Party of India (Option 3): A recognised national party as of September 2021.

 

• Bahujan Samaj Party (Option 4): A recognised national party as of September 2021.

question: ______, also known as search unemployment, occurs when workers lose their current job and are in the process of finding another one.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Frictional unemployment.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Frictional unemployment, also called search unemployment, occurs due to the time lag involved when workers move between jobs or enter the job market for the first time. (घर्षणात्मक बेरोजगारी)

 

• It is generally short-term/temporary in nature and exists even in a fully employed economy, since matching workers to suitable jobs takes time.

 

• It differs from structural unemployment, which arises from a mismatch between workers' skills and the requirements of available jobs.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Disguised unemployment occurs when more people are employed in an activity than are actually needed, common in Indian agriculture.

 

• Classical (real-wage) unemployment occurs when wages are kept above the market-clearing level, often due to minimum wage laws.

 

NOTE

 

• Voluntary unemployment (Option 1): Occurs when a worker chooses not to work at the prevailing wage rate.

 

• Disguised unemployment (Option 2): A situation where apparent employment exists, but the marginal productivity of some workers is close to zero.

 

• Classical unemployment (Option 4): Caused by wages set above the equilibrium level, often due to minimum wage laws or union bargaining.

question: Which of the following is NOT an application software?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Programming language translator software.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Application software is designed to help the user perform specific tasks (e.g., word processing, entertainment, education), while system software manages and operates the computer hardware itself.

 

• A programming language translator (compiler, interpreter, or assembler) converts source code into machine code — this is classified as System Software, not application software, since it supports the working of the computer system rather than performing an end-user task.

 

• Entertainment, education, and personal assistance software are all designed for end-user tasks and are examples of application software.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other examples of system software include operating systems, device drivers, and utility software.

 

• Common application software includes MS Word, MS Excel, web browsers, and media players.

 

NOTE

 

• Entertainment software (Option 1): Application software (e.g., games, media players).

 

• Education software (Option 2): Application software (e.g., e-learning tools).

 

• Personal assistance software (Option 4): Application software (e.g., calendar/reminder apps).

question: Which among the following lakes is known as the only "Floating Islands Lake" in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Loktak.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Loktak Lake, located in Manipur, is the largest freshwater lake in Northeast India and is famous for its floating masses of vegetation, soil, and organic matter called phumdis. (लोकटक झील — तैरता हुआ द्वीप)

 

• It is the only lake in India with a floating national park on it — the Keibul Lamjao National Park, the world's only floating national park, home to the endangered Sangai deer (brow-antlered deer).

 

• Loktak Lake was designated a Ramsar site (Wetland of International Importance) in 1990.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sangai (Manipur brow-antlered deer) survives in the wild only within Keibul Lamjao National Park.

 

• Loktak Lake plays a crucial role in Manipur's economy and ecology, supporting fisheries and hydroelectric power generation (Loktak Hydro Project).

 

NOTE

 

• Pulicat (Option 2): The second-largest brackish-water lagoon in India, located on the Andhra Pradesh–Tamil Nadu border.

 

• Chilka (Option 3): The largest brackish-water/coastal lagoon in India, located in Odisha.

 

• Kolleru (Option 4): A freshwater lake in Andhra Pradesh, situated between the Krishna and Godavari river deltas.

question: In India, what is the mean annual average temperature in subtropical vegetation zone?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 17°C to 24°C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's natural vegetation is classified based on climatic conditions, and one classification (by temperature zones) divides regions into tropical, subtropical, temperate, and alpine zones.

 

• The subtropical vegetation zone in India has a mean annual average temperature of about 17°C to 24°C, typically found in areas of moderate elevation.

 

• The tropical zone has a mean annual temperature above 24°C, the temperate zone ranges from about 7°C–17°C, and the alpine/tundra zone has temperatures below 7°C.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Subtropical vegetation includes subtropical broadleaved hill forests, subtropical pine forests, and subtropical dry evergreen forests, found in the sub-Himalayan tracts and peninsular hill areas.

 

• Vegetation zonation in India is primarily influenced by altitude, rainfall, and temperature.

 

NOTE

 

• Above 24°C (Option 1): Describes the tropical vegetation zone.

 

• 7°C to 17°C (Option 2): Describes the temperate vegetation zone.

 

• Below 7°C (Option 3): Describes the alpine vegetation zone.

question: Which famous sportsperson has received the Bharat Ratna award in 2014?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sachin Tendulkar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sachin Tendulkar, the legendary cricketer, was awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, in 2014 (announced in November 2013, conferred in February 2014). (भारत रत्न — सचिन तेंदुलकर)

 

• He became the youngest recipient of the Bharat Ratna and the first sportsperson to receive this honour.

 

• The award recognised his contribution to cricket, having scored 100 international centuries and being regarded as one of the greatest batsmen in the sport's history.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The eminent scientist C.N.R. Rao was also awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2014, alongside Tendulkar.

 

• As of the exam date, no other sportsperson besides Tendulkar had received the Bharat Ratna.

 

NOTE

 

• Ravi Shastri (Option 1): Former Indian cricketer and coach; not a Bharat Ratna recipient.

 

• Yogeshwar Dutt (Option 2): Olympic medal-winning wrestler; has not received the Bharat Ratna.

 

• MS Dhoni (Option 3): Former Indian cricket captain; has not received the Bharat Ratna (he received the Padma Bhushan in 2018).

question: What is India’s rank in reducing overall inequality according to the Commitment to Reducing Inequality Index (CRII) 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 123.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Commitment to Reducing Inequality Index (CRII) 2022, published by Oxfam and Development Finance International, ranked India 123rd out of 161 countries for its efforts to reduce inequality.

 

• India's rank improved by six places compared to the 2020 index, though it continued to perform poorly on health spending indicators.

 

• The index evaluates government action across three pillars: public services (health, education, social protection), taxation, and labour rights/wages.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Norway topped the CRII 2022 rankings as the best-performing country in reducing inequality.

 

• South Sudan ranked last (161st) in the 2022 index.

 

NOTE

 

• 118 (Option 1): Not India's CRII 2022 rank.

 

• 129 (Option 3): Not India's CRII 2022 rank.

 

• 132 (Option 4): Not India's CRII 2022 rank.

question: What is the atomic mass of sodium?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 23.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sodium (Na) has an atomic number of 11 and a standard atomic mass of approximately 23 u (22.99 g/mol). (सोडियम — परमाणु द्रव्यमान 23)

 

• It is a soft, highly reactive alkali metal belonging to Group 1 of the periodic table.

 

• Sodium's most common isotope is Sodium-23, which is stable and constitutes virtually all naturally occurring sodium.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sodium reacts vigorously with water to form sodium hydroxide and hydrogen gas.

 

• Common sodium compounds include sodium chloride (table salt) and sodium bicarbonate (baking soda).

 

NOTE

 

• 32 (Option 1): The approximate atomic mass of sulphur, not sodium.

 

• 40 (Option 2): The approximate atomic mass of calcium/argon, not sodium.

 

• 12 (Option 4): The approximate atomic mass of carbon (or atomic number of magnesium), not sodium's atomic mass.

question: Which Union Territory of India lies in the Bay of Bengal?
option_1: Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Andaman and Nicobar Islands is a Union Territory of India located in the Bay of Bengal, comprising over 570 islands. (अंडमान और निकोबार द्वीप समूह — बंगाल की खाड़ी)

 

• Its capital is Port Blair, and it lies close to Myanmar and Indonesia.

 

• The islands are of volcanic/tectonic origin and are separated from mainland India by the Bay of Bengal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lakshadweep, in contrast, lies in the Arabian Sea and is India's smallest Union Territory.

 

• The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are home to India's only active volcano, Barren Island.

 

NOTE

 

• Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu (Option 1): Located on India's west coast, along the Arabian Sea.

 

• Chandigarh (Option 2): A landlocked Union Territory in northern India, serving as the joint capital of Punjab and Haryana.

 

• Lakshadweep Islands (Option 3): Located in the Arabian Sea, not the Bay of Bengal.

question: Which of the following shortcut key is used to display the font dialog box in MS-Word 365?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ctrl + D.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In MS Word (including Word 365), the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + D opens the Font dialog box, which allows detailed formatting of font style, size, colour, and effects.

 

• This shortcut has remained consistent across various versions of MS Word.

 

• Ctrl + F is used to open the Find/Navigation pane, not the font dialog box.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ctrl + Shift + F and Ctrl + Shift + P are used to change the font and font size respectively in some contexts.

 

• Other common Word shortcuts: Ctrl+B (bold), Ctrl+I (italic), Ctrl+U (underline).

 

NOTE

 

• Ctrl + F (Option 1): Opens the Find dialog/navigation pane to search text.

 

• Alt + D (Option 3): Not a standard default shortcut for the font dialog box.

 

• Alt + F (Option 4): Typically activates the File menu/ribbon tab (File backstage view).

question: VSHORADS missile was successfully tested in September 2022 by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Defence Research and Development Organization (DRDO).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• VSHORADS (Very Short Range Air Defence System) is a man-portable air defence missile system developed by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO). (डीआरडीओ — रक्षा अनुसंधान एवं विकास संगठन)

 

• It is designed to neutralise low-altitude aerial threats such as helicopters and drones at short range, incorporating technologies like a miniaturised reaction control system and integrated avionics.

 

• The missile underwent successful flight trials, launched from a man-portable launcher off the coast of Odisha.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• DRDO is India's premier defence research agency (under the Ministry of Defence), responsible for developing missiles like Agni, Prithvi, Akash, and BrahMos (jointly with Russia).

 

• VSHORADS trials involved multiple successful test flights validating manoeuvrability and range performance.

 

NOTE

 

• ESSO (Option 2): The Earth System Science Organisation, under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, handles meteorology and earth-science research, not missile testing.

 

• HAL (Option 3): Hindustan Aeronautics Limited manufactures aircraft and helicopters, not missile systems like VSHORADS.

 

• FSI (Option 4): The Forest Survey of India conducts forest cover assessment, unrelated to defence technology.

question: Humayun’s Tomb situated in Delhi is built by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Biga Begum.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Humayun's Tomb in Delhi was commissioned by Bega Begum (also called Haji Begum or Biga Begum), the chief consort/widow of Mughal Emperor Humayun, around 1565–1572. (हुमायूँ का मकबरा — बेगा बेगम)

 

• It was designed by Persian architect Mirak Mirza Ghiyas and is considered the first grand Mughal garden-tomb, built in the charbagh (four-quartered garden) style.

 

• It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993 and served as an architectural precursor to the Taj Mahal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The tomb complex also houses the graves of several other Mughal royals.

 

• Humayun's Tomb underwent extensive restoration by the Aga Khan Trust for Culture in the 2000s–2010s.

 

NOTE

 

• Gulbadan Begum (Option 1): Daughter of Babur and sister of Humayun, author of "Humayun-Nama"; she did not commission the tomb.

 

• Hamida Begum (Option 3): Another wife of Humayun and mother of Akbar; not credited with commissioning the tomb.

 

• Maham Begum (Option 4): A wife of Emperor Babur and mother of Humayun; unrelated to building the tomb.

question: Which of the following statements is correct?
option_1: Living organisms can survive a wide range of pH change.
option_2: When pH of rain water is less than 8.2, it is called acid rain.
option_3: Our body works within the pH range of 7.0 to 7.8.
option_4: Tooth decay starts when the pH of the mouth is lower than 1.5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Our body works within the pH range of 7.0 to 7.8.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 3 is correct: various fluids in the human body function within a pH range of approximately 7.0 to 7.8 (blood itself is tightly regulated between 7.35–7.45, but 7.0–7.8 is the standard textbook range cited for the body's fluids overall).

 

• Statement 1 is incorrect: most living organisms, including humans, can survive only within a narrow pH range; large deviations disrupt enzyme activity and cellular functions.

 

• Statement 2 is incorrect: rainwater naturally has a pH of about 5.6 due to dissolved CO₂; rain is classified as acid rain when its pH falls below about 5.6, not 8.2.

 

• Statement 4 is incorrect: tooth decay (enamel demineralisation) begins when the pH of the mouth falls below about 5.5, not 1.5.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Human blood pH is tightly maintained between 7.35 and 7.45 by buffer systems.

 

• On the pH scale (0–14), 7 is neutral, values below 7 are acidic, and values above 7 are basic/alkaline.

 

NOTE

 

• Statement 1 (Option 1): False — organisms survive only within a narrow pH range.

 

• Statement 2 (Option 2): False — the acid rain threshold is a pH below about 5.6, not 8.2.

 

• Statement 4 (Option 4): False — tooth decay starts around pH 5.5, not 1.5.

question: Where was the Commonwealth games held in the year 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Birmingham.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2022 Commonwealth Games (22nd edition) were held in Birmingham, England, from 28 July to 8 August 2022. (बर्मिंघम — राष्ट्रमंडल खेल 2022)

 

• It was the third time England hosted the Commonwealth Games, after London (1934) and Manchester (2002).

 

• India finished 4th in the medal tally at the 2022 Commonwealth Games with 61 medals (22 gold, 16 silver, 23 bronze).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Birmingham 2022 was notable for featuring more medal events for women than for men, for the first time in Commonwealth Games history.

 

• The next Commonwealth Games (2026) is scheduled to be held in Glasgow, Scotland.

 

NOTE

 

• Gold Coast (Option 1): Host of the 2018 Commonwealth Games, Australia.

 

• New Delhi (Option 2): Host of the 2010 Commonwealth Games, India.

 

• Glasgow (Option 4): Hosted the 2014 Commonwealth Games; scheduled to host again in 2026.

question: Who among the following has been chosen as the male goalkeeper of the year by the International Hockey Federation (FIH) 2021-22?
solution_text:
The correct answer is PR Sreejesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• PR Sreejesh, India's veteran hockey goalkeeper, was named the FIH (International Hockey Federation) Male Goalkeeper of the Year for 2021, an award announced in early 2022. (पीआर श्रीजेश — एफआईएच वर्ष के सर्वश्रेष्ठ गोलकीपर)

 

• He is known for his crucial role in India's bronze medal win at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, the country's first Olympic hockey medal in 41 years.

 

• This award reaffirmed his standing as one of the world's top hockey goalkeepers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The FIH Awards recognise outstanding performances across categories such as Player, Goalkeeper, Rising Star, and Coach of the Year.

 

• Indian players like Harmanpreet Singh have also received FIH Player of the Year honours in subsequent years.

 

NOTE

 

• Mumtaz Khan (Option 2): An Indian women's hockey player recognised in young/rising-player categories, not the male goalkeeper award.

 

• Pirmin Blaak (Option 3): A Dutch hockey goalkeeper, a contender but not the 2021-22 winner.

 

• Arthur Thieffry (Option 4): A French hockey player, not the FIH Male Goalkeeper of the Year for 2021-22.

question: The shehnai is a reed instrument with how many holes along the tube?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Seven.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The shehnai is a classical Indian wind (reed) instrument, traditionally described as having seven holes along its tapering wooden tube, used for playing the melody by opening and closing them with the fingers. (शहनाई — सात छिद्र)

 

• It is a double/quadruple-reed conical instrument, generally made of wood, with a flared metal bell at the lower end.

 

• It is regarded as a "mangal vadya" (auspicious instrument) and is traditionally played at weddings and temple ceremonies in North India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ustad Bismillah Khan is the most celebrated shehnai player, credited with popularising the instrument internationally; he was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001.

 

• The shehnai is believed to have evolved from earlier reed instruments used in West Asia and South Asia.

 

NOTE

 

• Five (Option 1): Not the standard number of holes attributed to the shehnai.

 

• Eleven (Option 3): Not the standard number of holes attributed to the shehnai.

 

• Six (Option 4): Close to some variant descriptions, but not the standard textbook figure of seven.

question: The Indian National Congress was established when ______ delegates from all over the country met at Bombay in December 1885.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 72.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian National Congress (INC) was founded in December 1885, with its first session held at Bombay, attended by 72 delegates from across the country. (भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस — 72 प्रतिनिधि, 1885)

 

• The first session was presided over by Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee, and organised with the help of retired British civil servant Allan Octavian Hume.

 

• The INC later became the principal vehicle of India's freedom struggle against British colonial rule.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first INC session was originally planned for Pune but was shifted to Bombay due to a cholera outbreak.

 

• The second session of the INC (1886) was held in Calcutta under the presidency of Dadabhai Naoroji.

 

NOTE

 

• 34 (Option 1): Not the number of delegates at the first INC session.

 

• 108 (Option 3): Not the number of delegates at the first INC session.

 

• 156 (Option 4): Not the number of delegates at the first INC session.

question: ___________ is the change in total utility due to consumption of one additional unit of a commodity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Marginal utility (MU).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Marginal Utility (MU) is defined as the change in total utility resulting from the consumption of one additional unit of a commodity. (सीमांत उपयोगिता)

 

• According to the Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility, as a consumer consumes successive units of a good, the marginal utility derived from each additional unit tends to decline.

 

• MU can be calculated as MUₙ = TUₙ − TUₙ₋₁, where TU is total utility.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Total utility is the sum of the marginal utilities derived from consuming all units of a good.

 

• The concept of marginal utility underlies consumer equilibrium analysis in microeconomics.

 

NOTE

 

• Product Utility (PU) (Option 1): Not a standard recognised economic term for this concept.

 

• Revenue utility (RU) (Option 2): Not a standard recognised economic term for this concept.

 

• Demand utility (DU) (Option 3): Not a standard recognised economic term for this concept.

question: Which among the following pairs of 'animal – phylum of animal kingdom they belong' is incorrect?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Liver fluke - Nematoda.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The pairing "Liver fluke – Nematoda" is incorrect because the liver fluke (e.g., *Fasciola hepatica*) belongs to phylum Platyhelminthes (flatworms), specifically class Trematoda — not phylum Nematoda. (लिवर फ्लूक — प्लेटीहेल्मिन्थीज़ संघ)

 

• Phylum Nematoda (roundworms) includes organisms like *Ascaris*, *Wuchereria*, and *Ancylostoma* — the liver fluke is not among them.

 

• The other three pairings in the question are correct: Sycon belongs to Porifera (sponges), Prawns belong to Arthropoda, and Starfish belong to Echinodermata.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Phylum Platyhelminthes (flatworms) also includes tapeworms (*Taenia*) and planarians.

 

• Nematodes are characterised by a pseudocoelom and cylindrical, unsegmented bodies.

 

NOTE

 

• Sycon - Porifera (Option 2): A correct pairing; Sycon is a sponge genus under phylum Porifera.

 

• Prawns - Arthropoda (Option 3): A correct pairing; prawns are crustaceans under phylum Arthropoda.

 

• Starfish - Echinodermata (Option 4): A correct pairing; starfish belong to phylum Echinodermata.

question: Kalinga is the ancient name of coastal ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Orissa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kalinga is the ancient name of the coastal region of Odisha (Orissa), referring to the historical kingdom that flourished along India's eastern coast. (कलिंग — प्राचीन उड़ीसा)

 

• Kalinga is famously associated with the Kalinga War (261 BCE), fought by the Mauryan emperor Ashoka, whose immense bloodshed led to his conversion to Buddhism.

 

• The ancient Kalinga kingdom later saw the rise of rulers such as Kharavela of the Chedi dynasty.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kalinga War is considered a turning point in Indian history due to its influence on Ashoka's policy of Dhamma (moral governance).

 

• Present-day Odisha retains strong cultural links to ancient Kalinga, including in temple architecture (e.g., Konark, Puri).

 

NOTE

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 1): Ancient regions here included the Chola, Chera, and Pandya kingdoms, not Kalinga.

 

• Kerala (Option 3): Historically associated with the Chera dynasty, not Kalinga.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 4): Historically linked to the Satavahana and later Andhra kingdoms, not Kalinga.

question: The Arctic Ocean is located within the Arctic Circle and surrounds the North Pole. It is connected with the Pacific Ocean by a narrow stretch of shallow water known as ______ strait.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Berring.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Bering Strait (printed as "Berring" in the question) is a narrow strait connecting the Arctic Ocean with the Pacific Ocean, separating Russia (Siberia) from Alaska (USA). (बेरिंग जलसंधि)

 

• It is named after the Danish-Russian explorer Vitus Bering, who navigated the region in the 18th century.

 

• The Arctic Ocean, the smallest and shallowest of the world's oceans, is centred on the North Pole and is largely covered by sea ice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Bering Strait is believed to have served as a land bridge (Beringia) for early human migration from Asia to North America during the last Ice Age.

 

• The Arctic Ocean connects to the Atlantic Ocean via the Greenland Sea and Fram Strait.

 

NOTE

 

• Palk (Option 2): Connects the Palk Bay with the Bay of Bengal, situated between India (Tamil Nadu) and Sri Lanka.

 

• Hudson (Option 3): Connects Hudson Bay with the Atlantic Ocean in Canada, unrelated to the Arctic–Pacific connection.

 

• Bosphorus (Option 4): A strait connecting the Black Sea and the Sea of Marmara, separating Europe and Asia in Turkey.

question: Which among the following Ministries launched the app JALDOOT?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Rural Development.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The JALDOOT app was launched by the Ministry of Rural Development to enable systematic monitoring of groundwater levels across the country. (जलदूत ऐप — ग्रामीण विकास मंत्रालय)

 

• It is used by Gram Rozgar Sahayaks under the MGNREGA scheme to record water levels from designated observation wells twice a year (pre-monsoon and post-monsoon).

 

• The initiative supports groundwater management efforts, complementing schemes like the Atal Bhujal Yojana.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.
